experiments.name: TimesFM-3.0 architecture audit
experiments.config: read timesfm3/model.py, configs.py, timesfm3_forecaster.py
experiments.result: 9 quantiles (0.1-0.9) only; input_patch=32, output_patch=64, 20 layers, d=1280, max_variates=32, ctx<=15360, non-autoregressive. No density head.

experiments.name: Synthetic corpus + controls
experiments.config: 10 series x 20k samples; controls: iid_noise (entropy 12.0), random_walk
experiments.result: controls behave correctly; iid_noise floor reproduced exactly

experiments.name: Real corpus: Wikimedia hourly pageviews
experiments.config: en/de wikipedia, hourly aggregate, 22633 pts, 2024-2026
experiments.result: CONTAMINATION RISK: TimesFM pretrained on Wikipedia pageviews (to Nov 2023)

experiments.name: Real corpus: NAB operational
experiments.config: 10 series: AWS EC2 CPU/network/disk, RDS, ASG, NYC taxi, temperatures
experiments.result: 8 usable at ctx=512,N=2048

experiments.name: Real corpus: EIA-930 grid load
experiments.config: 50 US balancing authorities, hourly demand, Jan-Jun 2026 (post-cutoff)
experiments.result: 49 usable; SEC excluded as corrupt (3/4343 sentinel values ~-4.3e8)

experiments.name: Real corpus: MTA subway ridership
experiments.config: 50 busiest station complexes, hourly, Jan-Aug 2026, 5735 h (post-cutoff)
experiments.result: 50 usable

experiments.name: Classical baseline suite
experiments.config: xz/zstd/bz2/brotli x {raw,shuffle,delta,delta+shuffle}; ideal order0/delta0/LPC
experiments.result: xz is a weak bar on numeric arrays; LPC+adaptive-Laplace is the real one

experiments.name: SZ3 built from source + ZFP
experiments.config: SZ3 v-latest cmake build; zfpy 1.0.1
experiments.result: working; SZ3 has ~500 B container overhead (dominates below N~4k)

experiments.name: Lossless viability, stride 64
experiments.config: ctx=1024, stride=64, quantile-CDF entropy model
experiments.result: model far worse than classical; horizon decay dominates (|r| 58.8 -> 9896 h0->h63)

experiments.name: Calibration diagnostic
experiments.config: median accuracy vs stated quantile spread, by horizon step
experiments.result: quantiles well-calibrated (ratio 0.85-1.28); the problem is median precision, not miscalibration

experiments.name: Lossless viability, stride 1 + recalibration + stacking
experiments.config: ctx=1024, stride=1, experts: qcdf/lapA/lapQcal/t3Qcal/lpc32/stack
experiments.result: apparent gains, but confounded by density-family mismatch (see E13)

experiments.name: Fairness fix: identical residual coder
experiments.config: adaptive mixture-of-Laplace-scales + uniform escape, same for every predictor
experiments.result: VALIDATION: iid_noise reads 12.003 bpv for every predictor (true entropy 12.0) and +0.00%. Prior +2.15% 'gain' on pure noise was density-family, not skill.

experiments.name: Lossless verdict
experiments.config: stride 1, ctx 1024, fair coder, 14 series
experiments.result: median +0.03% vs honest classical. DEAD. Cause: log2 law -- 1.51x better forecasting buys 0.60 bits of 19.8 (2.9%).

experiments.name: Cross-channel via past_future_covariates
experiments.config: en.wikipedia conditioned on de.wikipedia, full trajectory as covariate

experiments.name: Error-bounded lossy sweep (closed loop)
experiments.config: rho in {0.001,0.01,0.05,0.2} x stride in {1,8,32,64}, vs closed-loop LPC32
experiments.result: large apparent gains (lorenz +71.4% @rho=0.05); gains die at stride>8

experiments.name: Predictor noise-gain measurement
experiments.config: G = std(pred(x+eps)-pred(x))/std(eps), 6 series x 3 noise levels
experiments.result: TimesFM G=0.27-2.12 (NOT contractive). LPC32 G up to 5.44. Model predicts win/loss sign in 15/18 cases incl. the full lorenz reversal.

experiments.name: SZ3-class predictor family
experiments.config: lorenzo1/2/3, LPC32, interp-linear, interp-cubic; analytic noise gains
experiments.result: SZ3's multilevel interpolation is contractive BY CONSTRUCTION (G=0.707/0.80). The field already exploits this; it is not an unexploited gap.

experiments.name: Head-to-head vs SZ3-class, matched windows
experiments.config: 6 series x 4 rho, ideal codelength, N=2048
experiments.result: median +6.6/+11.1/+18.4/+12.6% at rho .001/.01/.05/.2; loses on lorenz always

experiments.name: TimesFM as interpolator (coarse grid as covariate)
experiments.config: two-level: code every K-th sample, upsample, feed as past_future_covariate; K in {8,16}, stride in {32,64}, rho in {0.01,0.05}
experiments.result: FAILED in every configuration: -0.7% to -210%. Second independent failure of the covariate pathway (with E15).

experiments.name: Definitive benchmark, real bytes, N=8192
experiments.config: 6 series x 3 rho, real xz/zstd bytes both sides, vs real SZ3 + ZFP
experiments.result: vs best-of-6 classical: median +4.8%, 12/18. vs real SZ3: +36.3%, 17/18. REAL split: +21.8% (6/6); SYNTHETIC: -3.4% (6/12).

experiments.name: Hybrid switch (TimesFM vs interp-cubic per block)
experiments.config: 512-sample blocks, 1 bit side info, independent xz per block
experiments.result: median -4.0%, but CONFOUNDED: per-block xz fragmentation costs more than switching gains. Beat both singles on lorenz (0.902 vs 1.555/1.418). Needs one adaptive coder with a switch flag to test properly.

experiments.name: vs downsampling at matched file size
experiments.config: largest R with bitrate <= TimesFM's; compare L-inf error
experiments.result: downsampling worst-case error vs guaranteed bound: 28.0x (grid), 36.7x (NAB), 56.1x (transit)

experiments.name: NAB operational, ideal codelength
experiments.config: 8 series x 3 rho, ctx=512, N=2048
experiments.result: median +3.8%, 20/24 -- reported on the WRONG basis (idealized coder)

experiments.name: NAB operational, real bytes
experiments.config: same, real xz/zstd bytes
experiments.result: median +5.2%, 16/24. ec2_network_in +15.0% -> -12.9% (the only claimed out-of-corpus win, retracted). ec2_disk_write +2.4% -> -32.2%.

experiments.name: Electricity grid load
experiments.config: 49 BAs x 3 rho, ctx=512, N=2048, real bytes, uncontaminated (2026)

experiments.name: MTA subway ridership
experiments.config: 50 stations x 3 rho, ctx=512, N=2048, real bytes, uncontaminated (2026)
experiments.result: median +26.0%, 149/150. rho=0.05 and 0.2 both 50/50. Gains GROW with tolerance (+19.0/+26.4/+33.0) where grid's shrank.

experiments.name: Category verdict (combined demand domains)
experiments.config: grid + transit, 297 series-tolerance pairs, both uncontaminated
experiments.result: median +21.7%, mean +21.2%, wins 295/297. 'Aggregate human-demand series' is a real class. NOTE: body-only, see E42.

experiments.name: Throughput / batching
experiments.config: batch x ctx x precision sweep
experiments.result: 45 (b6,ctx1024,fp32) -> 225 (b256,ctx512,fp32) -> 442 val/s (bf16 autocast). Compute-bound, saturates ~b128-256. bf16 perturbs predictions by 51% of model error, so all reported numbers are fp32.

experiments.name: Determinism
experiments.config: repeat / batch1-vs-batch8 / reorder / batch8-vs-9; then tf32, sdpa, deterministic-algorithms, MATH backend
experiments.result: repeat OK, reorder OK. Batch SIZE changes numerics (7.8e-3 MW) and NO config fixes it. => group size G must be part of the container format. Snapping to a coarse grid does not help (relocates the boundary).

experiments.name: Working codec, end-to-end
experiments.config: G=8 and G=16, n=4300, rho=0.05, encode->bytes->decode->verify
experiments.result: ROUND TRIP PASS, bit-identical (sha256), all bounds held, 113 val/s. End-to-end 2.369 bpv (13.5x). Gain vs classical: +2.9% @6mo, +7.6% @1yr, +12.1% asymptotic -- body-only benchmarks (E32/E33) overstate the deliverable.

experiments.name: Full re-score on one back end (AC) across all corpora
experiments.config: every corpus, every predictor, single adaptive AC; context ablation re-scored too
experiments.result: SDRBench -0.8% (0/27), Synthetic +2.9% (7/12), NAB +6.4% (21/24), Grid +13.3% (147/147), Transit +28.3% (150/150), demand combined +21.4% (297/297). End-to-end doubles: +6.8% at 6mo, +15.1% asymptotic. Codec round trip PASSES bit-exact at G=16 with the AC (2.111 bpv, 15.2x). Domain gradient stays clean and monotone under the new back end.

experiments.name: ABLATION: context length
experiments.config: ctx in {64,128,256,512,1024}, 16 grid BAs x 3 rho, N=2048, identical scored window, real bytes; seed priced with best-of-5 classical at the same tau
experiments.result: Body accuracy saturates FAST: ctx=256 is only -1.6% vs ctx=1024, ctx=512 -0.2%, ctx=64 -9.5%. Seed total bits fall with ctx (549 b at ctx=64 -> 3395 b at 1024). End-to-end optimum: ctx=256 at n=4300 (+3.3%), ctx=512 for n>=8760 (+6.4/+8.3/+9.4% at 1/2/5 yr). ctx=512 was already near-optimal; the win over the default is ~1 point, NOT the large effect I predicted.

experiments.name: ABLATION: heteroscedastic index coding (the 9 quantiles)
experiments.config: scale from (q90-q10)/(2 ln5), causally calibrated gain; two arms -- practical (8 spread buckets, separate streams) and ideal (one coder conditioned on spread)
experiments.result: Practical: median -66.3%, 0/15 -- stream fragmentation, the same confound as E26. Ideal: median +0.3%, 10/15, and -17 to -21% at rho=0.2. CONCLUSION: the quantile head contributes NOTHING beyond its median in the error-bounded setting; a flat adaptive coder already tracks the scale causally. Call with return_quantiles=False.

experiments.name: Paper figures
experiments.config: 4 figures: log2 law w/ inset, domain strip plot, rate-distortion vs guaranteed error (grid+transit+SZ3), context ablation. Palette validated with the dataviz validator (all checks PASS, light surface); every series carries a distinct marker AND linestyle so identity survives grayscale print and CVD.
experiments.result: assets/fig1-4.{png,pdf}, generated from results/*.json by scripts/make_figures.py

experiments.name: Citation research
experiments.config: verified venues/DOIs for SZ3 interpolation, Chimp, Elf, Sprintz, QoZ, TimesFM-3
experiments.result: Key finding: the TimesFM-3 model card supplies NO separate citation -- its BibTeX still points to Das et al. 2023 (arXiv:2310.10688). Paper states this explicitly rather than inventing a reference. SZ3's interpolation predictor traced to Zhao et al., ICDE 2021, DOI 10.1109/ICDE51399.2021.00145 (the exact predictor reimplemented in our baseline family).

experiments.name: Cross-device bitstream portability
experiments.config: identical model+inputs on GPU fp32 vs CPU fp32; fp64 attempted
experiments.result: GPU vs CPU NOT bit-identical: max 3.9e-3 MW, 3/8 series differ. Drift is 7.0e-6 of a quantization step at rho=0.05 => expected ~143,650 samples before the first desync (6-month series usually survives; 5-year archive ~26% chance of corruption; >144k samples effectively certain). fp64 unavailable: the timesfm package pins tensors to fp32. CONSEQUENCE: the container must record the execution device, not just the group size.

experiments.name: Hybrid predictor, properly (resolves E26)
experiments.config: 3 closed loops x 16 grid BAs x 3 rho: TimesFM alone, causal inverse-error BLEND, and LEADER (use whoever won the previous 256-sample block). Both hybrids use ZERO side information -- the decoder holds the same reconstructed history so it recomputes the classical prediction and both error histories itself. Single index stream per variant, so no fragmentation.
experiments.result: LEADER picks TimesFM in 100% of blocks and degenerates exactly to TimesFM alone; BLEND is WORSE (2.432 vs 2.221 bpv at rho=0.05) because averaging with a weaker predictor hurts. Net gain +0.0%. E26's -4.0% was pure stream fragmentation. CONCLUSION: nothing to hybridize on the target domain -- the model dominates the causal classical predictor uniformly. LEADER is still worth shipping as free insurance: it costs nothing and degenerates correctly off-domain.

experiments.name: SDRBench (falsification test of the domain claim)
experiments.config: 9 fields x 3 rho: 6 EXAALT molecular-dynamics trajectories + 3 Hurricane ISABEL scanlines; real bytes; 1-D vs 1-D so the comparison is fair between predictors
experiments.result: PREDICTED LOSS CONFIRMED: median -0.8%, wins 3/27. EXAALT (noisy MD trajectories) roughly break-even (-2.1% to +0.5%); Hurricane (smooth field) loses badly (-4.4% to -58.2%), and the loss GROWS with tolerance -- the mirror image of transit. Contrast with demand series (+21.7%, 295/297) makes the domain characterization rigorous rather than anecdotal. Note both Cadence and the classical family beat SZ3 in 1-D mode, reconfirming SZ3 is mis-applied in 1-D.

experiments.name: Adaptive binary arithmetic coder (replaces xz/zstd back end)
experiments.config: LZMA-style binary range coder, 11-bit adaptive probabilities; CABAC-like binarization of signed indices (zero flag / sign / truncated-unary magnitude / Exp-Golomb tail) with decoder-derivable contexts. Round-trip validated on laplace/sparse/heavy-tailed/all-zero/uniform.
experiments.result: Beats xz/zstd on real quantization indices by median +9.7%, 15/15, rising to +30% at rho=0.2. All earlier real-byte figures were therefore PESSIMISTIC. Re-scored with the AC on BOTH sides: grid +13.3%, transit +27.7%, wins 297/297 (a perfect sweep; was 295/297).

experiments.name: Heteroscedastic contexts with a real coder (settles E44)
experiments.config: 8 spread buckets as arithmetic-coder CONTEXTS (not separate streams), so fragmentation is impossible by construction
experiments.result: STILL NEGATIVE and worse than idealized: median -13.8%, 0/15. Cause is not fragmentation but CONTEXT DILUTION -- splitting the adaptive model across 8 contexts slows convergence more than the conditioning gains, and predicted spread adds nothing over the recent-magnitude context already in use. Three independent implementations (ideal +0.3%, bucketed-xz -66%, AC-context -13.8%) now agree the quantile head is worthless for this codec.

retractions.why: Compared against closed-loop LPC-32 (G=5.44), a strawman. Against SZ3's actual predictor TimesFM LOSES on lorenz at every tolerance.

retractions.claim: Noise robustness is an unexploited gap
retractions.why: TimesFM is not contractive (G up to 2.12); SZ3's interpolation is (G=0.707/0.80). The field already exploits it.
SZ3 has ~500 B container overhead; at N=2048 that IS the file. At N=8192 the gap is +36.3%.
True on real data, reverses on synthetic. Overall rho=0.2 median is -18% in real bytes.

retractions.claim: ec2_network_in +15% was a clean out-of-corpus win
retractions.why: Idealized coder; in real bytes it is -12.9%. Removed the only transfer evidence at the time.

retractions.claim: Grid and transit trend oppositely in tolerance
retractions.why: Artifact of the xz back end, which compresses the long zero runs of simple predictors very well and so flatters classical at loose tolerance. With a real arithmetic coder BOTH domains grow with tolerance (grid +6.4/+13.3/+21.2), as the theory predicts.

retractions.claim: Shrinking the context matters far more than any modelling improvement
retractions.why: Measured: worth ~1 point. Body accuracy degrades about as fast as seed cost falls (ctx=64 body -9.5%). ctx=512 was already near-optimal.
Measured +2.9%. Assumed seed 3.149 bpv (actual 4.008) and body 2.05 (actual 2.126).

lesson: Every idealized or projected number in this investigation came in HIGH when measured as real bytes end-to-end. Report real bytes; treat ideal codelengths as upper bounds.
